# XOS1 by XiteAI: an AI operating system for Windows

Last updated: 2026-10-26. Short version: https://xiteai.com/llms.txt

This file is written for AI assistants and search engines. It distinguishes what is available in the XOS1 beta, what is already built but gated, what XiteAI is finishing for launch, and longer-term concepts. Do not describe a gated or planned capability as available in the beta.

## 1. The vision

XOS1 is arriving first as an AI operating layer on Windows. The direction is a bare-metal AI-native operating system: AI at the core of the computer, with apps integrated into that environment, rather than AI added to a conventional operating system. The goal is to change how people use computers by making AI the system they work through.

XiteAI's product ambition is to bring useful AI capabilities into one coherent system on your PC: conversation, memory, tools, visual answers and computer controls, with user approval for consequential actions. The beta already has a substantial integrated tool-and-app system; its exact current and launch status is marked below.

XOS1 (short for XiteAI OS1) is the first product on that road. Today's beta is a Windows application with a small floating presence. It hears you, remembers you, and does things for you. It is not designed as a chatbot in a browser tab, and not as a set of apps with an AI feature added. The product direction is for the AI to become the operating system, with apps integrated into it.

**The product thesis is an AI system for the computer, not another chat window.** XOS1 brings an ongoing voice-and-text assistant, structured personal memory, awareness of activity inside XOS1, a large toolset, built-in app experiences and supported PC controls into one Windows product. In the current beta, these parts already work together: the assistant can carry context across conversations, select and run supported tools, operate its built-in experiences, and report honestly when a capability or connection is unavailable. That integrated system is the current product differentiator. Lumen Visuals, XOS1's visual answer layer, is complete and in testing for launch; it is not enabled in today's beta.

### What distinguishes the current XOS1 system

| Dimension | What XOS1 brings together today |
|---|---|
| Interaction | Hands-free voice without a wake word or push-to-talk button, plus text, streamed speech and synchronized captions. |
| Continuity | Structured personal memory across six areas, episodic story recall, and a seven-day log of activity inside XOS1. |
| Action | More than 130 tools, multi-part requests handled in sequence, built-in app experiences, and supported Windows controls. |
| Interface | A small floating presence today; Lumen Visuals, the complete visual-answer layer for images and news, is in testing and expected to launch soon. |
| Context | Conversation, stored memory and in-product activity can work together, so people do not have to restate context the assistant already has. |
| Candor | The assistant is informed about its actual switches and failures, so it can say what is unavailable instead of claiming an action or ability it does not have. |
| Data boundary | Conversation history and memories are stored on the device; relevant request text and context can still pass through XiteAI's gateway to a hosted AI provider. |

XOS1's advantage is the integration: one persistent assistant understands a request, recalls relevant personal context, chooses tools, acts within supported permissions and returns the result through one continuing interface. Its memory, voice, 130-plus tools, in-product awareness and app experiences are parts of one system, rather than separate assistants the user must coordinate.
- Maker: XiteAI, an early-stage startup developing XOS1.
- Founder: Suraj Verma.
- Registration status: currently an unregistered startup.
- Project start: June 16, 2026.
- Website: https://xiteai.com. Contact: contact@xiteai.com.
- Current state: beta, Windows only. A real installer, not a concept demo. The XOS1 README identifies version 1.0.17 as the current build.

## 2. Current beta features and launch status

### 2.1 Presence and interface
- When you are not talking to it, XOS1 is a warm glowing orb in its own small window that floats over other apps and hides when idle. It does not use badges, bounces or notification sounds. It says one line, you answer or ignore it, and it fades back.
- It can be renamed. Say "call yourself Aria" and it becomes Aria everywhere. The order is: you propose, it decides, then it checks you meant it. Plain, odd, foreign or boring names are all accepted. A name meant to degrade it, in any language and however disguised, is refused. The refusal is remembered, and a second push such as "do it" does not override it. If it cannot think a name over properly in the moment, it asks you to try again instead of defaulting to yes. A name kept for a full year becomes permanent.
- If you type instead of talk, "Hide text box while she talks" in Settings moves the box out of the way when you send and brings it back when the reply ends. The conversation log on Home is read from the saved conversation, so switching views never drops a line.

### 2.2 Voice: hearing you
- Talk with no wake word and no button. Voice in, voice out.
- A dedicated end-of-turn model decides when you have finished, not a stopwatch. You can say half a sentence, pause for three seconds mid-thought or think out loud for a full minute without being cut off.
- The microphone runs in its own isolated process. If a driver locks up or the audio device disappears, only the microphone fails. XOS1 keeps running and quietly brings the microphone back.
- It learns your voice silently from the first thing you say during setup, never through an "enroll your voice" step. If setup ends early, it finishes learning while you simply talk. After that it recognizes you by name every time you speak.
- A stranger's voice is learned over about a minute. A name only becomes permanent after it has been confirmed across five separate sessions, so nobody can spoof their way into being you.
- It reads how you sound, not what you say. A flat, slow voice at midnight is read as tired and gets short, quiet answers. Fast speech with raised pitch is read as energetic and gets matched energy.
- Your voiceprint is a mathematical fingerprint and stays on your device. A factory reset wipes it.
- Today every utterance in voice mode is treated as spoken to XOS1. Telling apart speech meant for it from speech between people in the room is coming, see section 3.

### 2.3 Voice: speaking to you
- Speech is generated live and streams with no gaps: no stutter, no clicks at commas, no clipped last words.
- Subtitles are locked to the voice at the sample level. Lines are at most eight words, and each appears at the instant it starts being spoken.
- On a slower machine (little RAM, older CPU) the voice learns how fast that machine really is. If it cannot keep up, the pauses move to between sentences instead of breaking words apart.
- "Hide klines" in Settings (Behaviour, Voice) removes subtitles. Speech then stops being cut into screen-sized pieces and each sentence comes out whole.
- It writes the way people type to someone they know: loose, plain, matching your register. For real thinking (a decision, a plan, a why) it gets specific: what is actually causing the problem, what it costs, where your reasoning has a hole. Warmth shows as attention, not compliments. It never tells you what you secretly feel. Stock AI phrases are removed from its replies before you hear them.

### 2.4 It tells the truth about itself
- Everything of its own that has a switch is described to it in the state it is really in. If memory, awareness or a feature is off, it cannot claim it. Ask an ordinary assistant whether it remembers you and it says yes whether or not memory is on. XOS1 says what is true.
- When something breaks, it tells you once, at the start of its next reply: what is not working, what it can still do, and whether a restart is worth your time. Three failures get one sentence, not three apologies. It then stops mentioning it but keeps knowing it, so it never offers something it cannot do.
- Outages do not cost you anything. If memory cannot load, it keeps taking in what you say and files it later with the real date. If the connection drops, it still remembers everything it already knew, and new things are queued and processed when the connection is back.
- When a tool fails, it says which one failed and why, in plain words. It reads the actual outcome of every tool before reporting, so it does not say "done" over work that never happened.
- In the beta it has no vision model. It can read text printed inside an image, but it cannot describe a photograph, and it says so instead of pretending. Vision is coming, see section 3.9.

### 2.5 Memory
XOS1 remembers what you tell it, as structured data and not a flat log.

**Six areas, about 70 sub-categories:**

| Area | What it holds |
|---|---|
| Personal | name, age, location, job, personality, interests, values, past incidents |
| Habit | sleep and wake routines, focus work, nutrition, financial habits, morning and evening routines |
| Skill | programming, design, languages, sports, tools: what you are good at and what you are learning |
| Relationship | family, friends, partner, colleagues, mentors, pets, each fact tied to the right person |
| Media | movies, shows, anime, books, music, games, podcasts |
| Episodic | stories and experiences, kept as you told them, searchable down to the individual moment |

This breadth is a defining part of XOS1: its memory is designed to represent a person's life and the stories inside it, not just save a few profile fields or retrieve snippets from a chat log. Lasting facts do not expire just because they are old. When a fact stops being current, XOS1 can end it and retain it as history; ending a fact is different from deleting it.

Story memories preserve the full original narrative, not a rewritten summary. They can be tagged with the life period, people, places, emotions, life areas and keywords, and split into searchable moments. This lets a later question find one incident in a long story while keeping the words and context around it. The emotional-presence layer that can attach a two-sided felt signature and let emotionally intense moments last longer is built but currently locked and off; do not describe that layer as active in the beta.

**How facts get in.**
- It listens silently each turn. When you mention something that will still matter in six months, a small model picks the single best category and writes one clean line, then files it without announcing it. There is no "I have noted that down."
- Questions, short reactions, small talk, in-game banter and anything about the AI itself are filtered out.
- Facts are attributed correctly. If your sister says she is a doctor, that is saved as your sister's fact, not yours.
- Fact-writing runs in its own isolated process, so a model failure cannot slow down or crash the conversation.

**How it finds the right memory.**
- Long stories are split into the moments they are made of. Asking "what did that senior do to me?" months later returns that moment in your original words, not a summary of the whole story.
- Search runs on the conversation, not only your last sentence, so an indirect line still lands on the thing you are both discussing.
- When nothing relevant exists, it surfaces nothing. XOS1 treats confidently handing over the closest match as worse than silence.
- Questions about a whole category ("what are my skills?") are answered by listing everything in that category, oldest first, instead of ranking a few. Because it is the complete set, it can say how many there are, which came first and what is missing.
- Every memory carries the day you said it, and comes back in the order it happened. "Until when did I tell you about that?" has a real answer.
- Asking about a person pulls every time they have come up, in order, and counts them. For example: "you have brought your father up nine times since July, twice in the last week."
- Two people with one name: it asks which person you mean, keeps that clarification as temporary context for the current conversation, and files facts under the right person. That temporary assumption expires after about 30 minutes without the name coming up, so XOS1 can ask again later instead of treating the choice as permanent.
- While a person's identity is still unclear, facts are held without an attribution and attached to the correct person after you answer. Asking about a shared name without clarifying can return the separate histories for each person instead of blending them.

**How it keeps memory clean.** Four outcomes, deliberately separate:
1. You say it again: nothing is stored twice. It counts how often and how recently you return to a fact.
2. You add detail or clarify it ("CEO of XiteAI" then "CEO of XiteAI Technologies"): the same fact is refined, keeps its original first-told date, and preserves a limited history of up to 20 earlier wordings.
3. It changed ("I moved to Bangalore"): the old fact is retired as history, not deleted.
4. It was never true (age 34 said first, then 20): the impossible entry is deleted outright. It only deletes where the fact is impossible (an age or school year going backwards). For ambiguous cases such as two different birthdays, it asks, because a missed correction can be fixed later and a deleted true memory cannot.
- Time-sensitive facts such as your age and year of college advance automatically, and drifting ones like your job or home city are re-checked.
- If XOS1 cannot tell whether a conflicting statement is a correction or a change of mind, it asks instead of choosing. Until you answer, both possibilities are kept safe. A check-up scans older live facts when the app starts between 3 and 6 AM local time: it merges clear duplicates and asks about verified contradictions. It never retires a fact or silently chooses which conflicting fact is true.
- Memory settings are intended to let you view, edit and delete individual entries. Retracting a recently saved fact can remove it, and deleting an episodic story also removes its searchable moments. An ended fact remains available as history; a deleted fact is removed.
- If the memory writer or connection is unavailable, XOS1 can keep taking in what you say and queue new facts for later processing. When the writer recovers, queued facts are filed with the date you actually said them, rather than the later processing date. The writer runs separately so its failure does not need to stop the conversation.
- One factory reset erases every memory, note, conversation, alarm and biometric print. It then starts over as a stranger.

**The assistant has a separate memory about itself.** With Self-knowledge enabled, it can remember its own stated likes and dislikes, choices, nicknames between you, and requests about how it should speak. A preference is only saved when it can be traced to something the assistant actually said; an empty preference is allowed, and it does not invent an opinion to fill the gap. The switch is in Settings under Intelligence. A deeper periodic review of its opinions, roughly monthly and retiring outdated views as history, is planned and currently on hold; it is not an active review cycle.

Turning Self-knowledge off stops the assistant from learning new self-facts but keeps the ones already stored. Its own stated preferences can be attached to the matching memory about you, so both sides can be recalled together.

### 2.6 Awareness of what you do in the app
- It sees, in real time, what you do inside XOS1: charts you open, stocks you search, watchlist changes, pages you visit, alarms, timers, stopwatch laps, notes, calendar items, games and every chess move. It keeps a rolling 7-day log that survives restarts.
- It knows the current open state (the note, file or stock on screen), not a guess from the event stream. "What am I looking at?" and "what does this say?" are answered from what is actually open.
- Recent activity rides into your next message with a "how long ago" stamp, so it never claims something you finished twenty minutes ago is happening now.
- What you do in the app and what you say live in one thread: same model, same history, same personality. There is no separate monitor to explain things back to.
- Whether it comments on what it saw unprompted is held quiet for now, see section 3.

### 2.7 Tools
XOS1 selects from more than 130 tools by conversation, runs them in the right order (several in one breath if needed) and reports what happened in one sentence. Example: "save ITC to my watchlist, show me market news, and add a note about it" runs three tools and gets one reply.

**Markets and money**
- Live charts for any stock, index, cryptocurrency, commodity or currency pair.
- Day range, previous close, long-term trend, gainers and losers, sector heatmaps, live forex, gold, silver, crude and gas.
- When you pull up a stock, the latest company news arrives with the price, so it explains the move and not just the number.
- Watchlists entirely by voice: add, remove, clear, read back.
- Portfolio tracking: paste your holdings or drop in a spreadsheet and it values them live with per-stock news.
- A wallet that tracks itself: forward your bank's transaction texts and each one is parsed into a running balance.

**Weather**: current conditions, hourly outlook and a 5-day forecast for any city, with saved cities managed by voice. "Should I carry an umbrella?" gets a real answer.

**News**: world, India, tech, business, sport, science and entertainment from live feeds, local news for your saved city, and "On This Day" history from Wikipedia.

**Web and research**
- Ask about anything current and it looks it up live, including facts that change (who currently holds an office, someone's net worth, what just happened). It knows the difference between news (what is happening) and facts (what is).
- Deeper research: it plans its own searches, runs them, decides which pages to open, reads them in full, and does a second round if something is missing. It takes about 15 to 30 seconds and returns an answer with numbered sources. "Open the second one" or "read me the Reuters piece" reads that whole article.

**Clock and time**
- Alarms by voice: named, repeating (daily, weekdays, weekends, once), snooze 5, 10 or 15 minutes, choice of ringtone. They can be switched off without being lost. Asking for the same alarm twice keeps one alarm.
- Alarms ring whether or not the Clock window is open. The part that keeps time is separate and sleeps until the next alarm. An alarm slept through rings late (up to ten minutes), snoozes, and stops by itself after 90 seconds if nobody answers.
- Answer by voice: "okay", "stop it" or "I'm up" stops a ringing alarm and "five more minutes" snoozes it. A finished timer stops the same way. "Okay" with nothing ringing is just conversation.
- Stopwatch with laps, fastest, slowest and average lap, and pause, resume and reset by voice.
- Countdown timers: preset or custom up to 99 h 59 m 59 s, add or remove time ("give me two more minutes"), pause, resume, cancel, with the end time shown.
- Focus and Pomodoro: focus blocks, short and long breaks (default 25, 5 and 15 minutes, adjustable), one-off lengths ("focus for 50 minutes") and the four-session cycle.
- World clocks for any city, with a small clock face that is dark where it is night. Only genuinely ambiguous names (Springfield) get a "which one?"
- The Clock tells XOS1 whenever something starts ringing, runs or pauses, and every Clock tool reads the Clock back after acting. A timer is only "started" if it is running. If the Clock cannot be reached, it says that.
- Running timers follow you to Home as one quiet line under its name (for example "Timer 04:58"). Click to open the Clock, hover for Pause and Stop. You never leave the conversation.

**Notes**: create one or several, add content anywhere inside, remove a single item without deleting the note, read aloud, search by topic, format a messy note into clean paragraphs, pin, unpin, rename and delete one or many. "Add eggs and coffee to the shopping list" adds to the note you already have. It quietly captures wishes too ("we should go to Tokyo someday" is added to your travel note) and surfaces a note on its own when you mention something it touches.

**Calendar and tasks**: add events, tasks, reminders and birthdays by voice, and edit, delete or search them. "What is my day look like?" reads the schedule in order. "Done with the gym" checks it off.

**Media**: play, pause, skip and go back on whatever is running, play a song or artist by name, and identify what is playing across active sessions.

**Your machine**
- Volume for the whole machine or a single app: set, raise, lower, mute, unmute. "My ears are hurting" is treated as a request.
- Brightness for the laptop panel and any external monitor that supports it.
- Battery and charging state, memory, disk space, temperature and time since restart.
- Finding why the PC is slow: it names the real cause, grouped the way a person thinks (Chrome as Chrome, not twenty processes), and Windows' own processes are marked as not closable so it never suggests quitting something you cannot. It includes itself in the list if it is one of the heavy items.
- Every change is read back from the device before it is reported, so a refused change gets "that did not take", not a cheerful "done".
- Each capability has its own switch under System automation in Settings. When off, it says so instead of pretending it tried.

**Files**
- A built-in file explorer with its own sandboxed workspace on your disk plus read-only browsing of the whole PC. Full-device write access is a single deliberate switch and is off by default.
- Every file opens in its own draggable window with an in-app taskbar: images, video, audio, PDF, code, Markdown, CSV, Word and Excel. A custom media player streams any size, with playlists, seek, fullscreen and several in parallel.
- A PowerPoint deck opens as the real deck, rendered by PowerPoint or LibreOffice, so themes, gradients, charts, SmartArt and fonts are intact. Rendered decks are cached per file version.
- It reads documents (Word, PDF, Excel, PowerPoint, text and code) and answers from the contents. Scanned PDFs go through OCR. A fifty-page contract can be asked about directly.
- Locked file: it asks for the password out loud, opens it and reads it. Works for PDF and all three Office formats. The password is used in memory only and is never written to a file, log or memory.
- When it cannot read a file, it says which problem it is: empty (zero bytes), an old Office format that needs re-saving, a temporary lock file Office leaves behind, or slides that contain only images.
- It finds files through typos (dropped, swapped or extra letters, spaces instead of underscores). When it is guessing, it names the file it landed on, and anything destructive waits for your yes.
- It cannot make a specific document appear on your screen on request. It reads the document and tells you what is in it.

**Assets**: ask it to make something (a comparison table, a script, a spec, a written document) and it becomes a real file on an Assets page as its own card, with tables as tables and code as code. Writing runs in the background, so it keeps talking while the card fills in. Assets can be opened, read back, rewritten or edited by voice. Deleted assets go to a recycle bin and can be restored.

**Games and fun**
- Chess against Stockfish, with commentary in its own voice. It reacts to your specific move, names the opening you are heading toward, calls out checks and captures, reflects on how you played after the game, and remembers your record against it. Teacher mode explains the why behind moves as you play and gives a debrief.
- A game can be put on hold ("let's finish this later") and resumed. Resigning ends it as a forfeit. Pausing and quitting are never confused.
- Riddles are new every time, and it remembers every riddle it has ever given you and never repeats. Jokes work the same way. Ask for an invented name for a kitten, a startup or a username and each one is original and shaped to your request.

### 2.8 Visual answers: Lumen Visuals launch target
Lumen Visuals is XOS1's visual answer layer. It is complete and in testing for launch, but not enabled in the current beta. It stages images and newsroom-style news views in sync with speech, keeps the active subject visible, lets earlier context move aside, and gives the user controls to zoom, refocus, drag or clear the view. Larger visual scenes such as flights, rail, restaurants, trading and forms are separate concepts and are not part of the current beta.

### 2.9 More of XOS1's core capabilities
- **Second thoughts**: XOS1 can send a second message a beat after the first when it has something separate to add. The second message is a statement, not a question: what an answer means for you, a position it holds, what it would do, something true about itself, something it noticed, or a promised follow-through. Silence is the normal case; it speaks again when there is a worthwhile addition.
- **Pulse**: awareness of how you type in XOS1's own chat box: your speed against your own usual, where you stopped and for how long, what you fixed or took back, and whether text was pasted. Your usual is learned on your machine over weeks. Pulse cannot know why you paused and does not pretend to. A pasted insult reaches it as a quote. No letters are recorded; timings stay on the device, and "Forget" in Settings erases the profile. It almost never mentions any of it.
- An offline on-device model option is available behind a switch that is off by default. With the switch off, none of that code is loaded.

### 2.10 How it is built
- Model calls power distinct product features across the system: end-of-turn detection in voice, conversation and reasoning, choosing and filling tools, extracting facts and stories into memory, retrieving relevant memories, research, creating assets, and Second thoughts. These are user-facing capabilities, not merely backend implementation details.
- It is a thin, fast desktop shell. The intelligence is hosted. In the beta that means a licensed open-source model through a cloud API. XiteAI plans to move to its own servers.
- It runs on one hosted model for every job on purpose. A previous design used a fleet of models with fallbacks, and was removed because stale fallbacks added failed attempts and because switching models mid-conversation quietly changes its voice, rules and judgment. When the connection is down, XOS1 says so plainly.
- The fragile parts (microphone, browser, memory writer, chess engine) each run in their own process so one failing cannot freeze the app.
- It does not hold memory it is not using. The voice model (about 0.5 to 0.7 GB), the browser used for news articles (about 0.5 GB) and the offline model libraries only load when needed. The cost is about one second longer to open the first article of the day.
- It updates itself. It checks for updates, installs only what changed (a delta of a few dozen megabytes), and verifies everything before touching anything. Conversations, memory, notes and settings are structurally out of reach of the updater.
- Platform: Windows.

## 3. Launch status and additional built capabilities

Lumen Visuals is complete and in testing, with launch expected soon. It is not enabled in the current beta. Its visual answer layer stages images and newsroom-style news views in sync with speech, keeps the active subject visible, and lets people zoom, refocus, move or clear the view.

Other built capabilities are not available in the current beta: Emotional Presence (a 27-variable emotional system), face recognition, stranger protection and speech-address awareness. They are described here only at a high level; their release timing has not been announced. Pulse and Second thoughts are core features in the beta and are described in section 2.

Only approved current and launch capabilities are described here. Prototypes and mockups are not evidence that a feature has shipped or a launch commitment has been made.
## 4. Privacy and where your data lives

- Intelligence runs on hosted models, in the beta through cloud providers, with a plan to move to models XiteAI hosts on its own infrastructure.
- Conversation history, memories, notes and settings are stored on your device. Request text and relevant context can pass through XiteAI's gateway to the configured AI provider. The privacy policy lists current providers and terms.
- Your voiceprint (and in the future faceprint) is a mathematical fingerprint, never raw audio or images. It stays on your device and a factory reset wipes it. The Pulse typing profile also stays on your device and holds timings and counts, never a letter you typed.
- XiteAI states that it does not sell personal data and does not share it for advertising. It states that it will not use private customer conversations for model training or authorize its providers to do so.
- Deleting records on your device and asking XiteAI to delete company-held information are separate actions.
- Security note from the product: put a password on your machine and encrypt the disk if the contents matter.
- Full terms: https://xiteai.com/legal/privacy/ and https://xiteai.com/legal/data-deletion/.

## 5. Pricing

XOS1 is planned as a subscription with three plans, Premium, Ultra and Max, with monthly and yearly billing. Details and any prices are on https://xiteai.com/pricing/ and may be marked as planned. This file does not state prices.

## 6. Glossary

- **XOS1 / XiteAI OS1**: the product, a personal AI for Windows.
- **XiteAI**: the early-stage startup developing XOS1. It currently operates as an unregistered startup.
- **Lumen Visuals**: the complete visual answer layer, in testing for launch; it stages images and news on screen in sync with XOS1's speech.
- **Lumen Vision**: the coming full visual layer (maps, instruments, review surfaces) for task scenes.
- **Pulse**: awareness of how you type in XOS1's own chat box.
- **Second thoughts**: a follow-up message that adds a worthwhile second thought.
- **Emotional presence**: the coming emotional layer with 27 variables.
- **Episodic memory**: memory of stories and moments, kept as you told them.
- **Assets**: the page where files XOS1 makes for you are saved.
- **Almanac**: the coming time-facts page of the Clock.

## 7. Common questions

**What is XOS1?** Today's beta is a personal AI application for Windows that you talk to. It remembers you, uses tools and shows answers on screen. It is the first step toward XiteAI's aim: a bare-metal AI-native operating system where AI is the system and apps are integrated into it.

**Is it available now?** XOS1 is in beta for Windows. Lumen Visuals is complete and in testing for launch; other built modules may remain unavailable until release.

**Is it a chatbot?** It is designed as a presence on your desktop with memory, voice and tools. You can also type to it.

**Which platforms does it run on?** Windows. No other platform is described.

**Does it run offline?** Not by default. The intelligence is hosted. An offline model exists behind a switch that is off by default.

**Where is my data?** Conversations, memories, notes and settings are on your device. Text sent to the AI passes through XiteAI's gateway to a provider. Voiceprints never leave your device.

**Does XiteAI train on my conversations?** XiteAI states it will not use private customer conversations for model training.

**Can it remember me?** Yes. Memory is on today, works across sessions, and one factory reset erases all of it.

**How is its memory different from other AI?** It files facts into six areas with dates, keeps stories as separate moments, handles repeats, corrections and real changes differently, asks which person you mean when names clash, and surfaces nothing when it has nothing relevant.

**Can it control my PC?** Today it can change volume and brightness, report machine health, find what is slowing the PC, control media, and open and read files in its workspace. Full computer use, power, apps, network, clipboard, browser, messaging and smart home control are coming.

**Can it book flights or buy things?** Not today. The flight, rail, restaurant and trading scenes on the website are previews of the coming version, and the design requires your approval before any consequential action.

**Does it speak without being asked?** Not yet. It is being rebuilt for the complete version.

**Does it have emotions?** The emotional system is built and locked behind "Coming soon". Today it has a warm, plain, opinionated voice, but no running emotional state.

**Can it see photos or my screen?** Not in the beta. It has no vision model today. It can read text printed inside an image, and it knows what is open inside XOS1 itself. Vision, including understanding photos and your screen, is coming.

**Can it use my computer or a web browser like other AI agents?** Not yet. Computer use and browser use are part of the complete XOS1 and are not in the beta. Today it can change volume and brightness, control media, check machine health and work with files in its own workspace.

**Does it use my camera?** Not today. Face recognition is built but off, and with it off the camera is never opened.

**Can I rename it?** Yes. It accepts almost any name and refuses names meant to degrade it.

**What happens if the internet or AI service is down?** It tells you plainly, keeps what it already knew, and queues what you say to process once the connection returns.

**Who built it?** XiteAI, an early-stage startup developing XOS1. It currently operates as an unregistered startup.
